mission.cluster: deterministic research statistics and the research experiment battery

adaptation: TypeScript -> plain ESM JavaScript, Node 24, no dependencies. Both donor files carry no import at all, and neither ported file imports anything outside this directory. Function names, formulae, rounding, NaN guards, array ordering, field ordering, default parameters and every string literal are the donor's; the donor's two file boundaries are kept as `statistics.mjs` and `battery.mjs`, with `contracts.mjs` holding the frozen vocabularies/thresholds/validators and `index.mjs` the single export site.

The donor's type-only declarations become frozen runtime vocabularies in `contracts.mjs`: RESEARCH_DOMAINS is the donor's exported const member for member, RESEARCH_TERMINAL_STATUSES materialises the ResearchTerminalStatus union, REPLICATION_STATUSES and REVIEW_STATUSES materialise the two inline unions on ResearchEvidence, and the donor's own (declared but unread) READY_GATES const is carried unchanged. No member and no order is new.

The donor's numeric defaults become named frozen thresholds with the donor's exact values: DEFAULT_CI_Z 1.96, DEFAULT_BOOTSTRAP_SEED 42, DEFAULT_BOOTSTRAP_SAMPLES 1000, DEFAULT_BOOTSTRAP_ALPHA 0.05, DEFAULT_PERMUTATIONS 5000, DEFAULT_ONE_SAMPLE_PERMUTATION_SEED 11, DEFAULT_PERMUTATION_SEED 7. Each is consumed exactly where the donor wrote its literal, including the paired branch of `permutationP`, which passes `options.seed` through to the private helper and so inherits 7 rather than 42.

The value shapes are copy-on-construct factories and the single validation gate: `researchEvidence` and `researchOutcomeInput` check the donor's declared shape (all nine ResearchEvidence fields as booleans/enums, domain in the five domains, declaredStatus in the five terminal statuses, hypothesisSupported boolean-or-null) and return a new object in the donor interface's field order. A factory never repairs: a missing, mis-typed or out-of-vocabulary value is refused with a TypeError instead of being defaulted, coerced or clamped.

`adjudicateResearchOutcome` is deliberately NOT gated by those factories. The donor's final branch reports an undeclared terminal status explicitly ('unknown declared status <value>'), and putting the factory in front of it would delete that branch. The contracts gate callers that construct an input; adjudication keeps the donor's runtime tolerance, including its acceptance of a partial evidence object.

`standardDeviation(values, sample = true)` keeps both the sample and population forms with the donor's length thresholds (n < 2 and n < 1); `median` keeps the sort of a copy so the caller's array is never reordered; `permutationPairedP` stays module-private exactly as the donor left it and is reached through `permutationP({ paired: true })`.

There is nothing to inject: the donor reads no clock, generates no id, opens no file, reads no environment and calls no network, and neither does the port. The only generator is the donor's own seeded `mulberry32`, so the same input and seed always produce the same number.

`buildResearchBattery`'s local `full()` helper still supplies the donor's complete §34 chain, now materialised through `researchEvidence`, so an invalid scenario would fail loudly at construction. The six scenarios' domains, declared statuses, hypothesis values, evidence overrides and labels are the donor's.
knownDifferences: No research conductor, no experiment execution, no protocol store, no persistence, no provider call and no manuscript or review pipeline: those are explicitly out of scope. The existing `evidence-engine` module owns evidence and is neither imported, re-exported, wrapped nor forked here.

The donor's READY path can never actually return REPLICATION_FAILED: its downgrade tests `missing.some((item) => item.includes('replication'))`, and no label the missing list can hold contains the substring 'replication'. The branch is carried verbatim and is unreachable, rather than removed or rewritten.

A declared READY is never checked against `replication`: the donor's READY_GATES has no replication member, so a READY over a FAILED or NOT_ATTEMPTED replication still returns status READY with pass true. Recorded as the donor's own gap; not tightened.

`REJECTED` and `REPLICATION_FAILED` both require the replication to have been recorded, but `replication` is not one of the labels pushed into `missing`, so an unrecorded replication fails with the donor's reason ending in `missing: ` (empty list, trailing space). Kept byte for byte.

`INCONCLUSIVE` reads only executionEvidence and statistics, and `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` reads only protocol and executionEvidence: in the donor a vetoed review, a missing manuscript or an unrecorded replication does not block those two PASS paths, and it does not block them here.

`bootstrapCi`'s quantile indices are floor(alpha/2 * samples) and ceil((1 - alpha/2) * samples) - 1. For alpha = 1 the lower index exceeds the upper, so the returned interval has lower > upper (for example [1,2,3,4] at 4 samples gives 2.75 / 2.25). The donor returns the pair in that order and does not sort it into sense; neither does the port.
The donor declares READY_GATES and never reads it. It is carried as a frozen vocabulary in `contracts.mjs` and is not wired into a rule the donor did not write, so it has no effect on any verdict.

`researchEvidence`/`researchOutcomeInput` are a new construction-time gate the donor did not have (its TypeScript interfaces were compile-time only). They change no result for any input a ported function accepts: `adjudicateResearchOutcome` is not behind them, and every scenario the donor's own battery builds passes them unchanged.

The donor's type declarations (ResearchEvidence, ResearchOutcomeInput, ResearchBatteryVerdict, ResearchDomain, ResearchTerminalStatus) have no runtime artefact beyond the frozen vocabularies and the two factories; a verdict is the plain object the donor returned, with `domain`, `declaredStatus`, `status`, `pass`, `reason` and `missing` in the donor's order.

The donor's comments claiming a 95% CI and a §34 chain are kept as documentation, but no statistic is rounded and no confidence level is verified: `confidenceInterval` returns the raw floating-point pair, and the tests pin the unrounded values (for [1,3] at n = 2, lower is 0.040000000000000036).

vectors: mean is sum/n and NaN for an empty sample; median sorts a copy and averages the two middle values for an even count (V8 = [2,4,4,4,5,5,7,9] gives mean 5 and median 4.5)
standardDeviation is the sample form (n - 1) by default and NaN below two values, the population form (n) and NaN below one value when sample = false; V8 gives 2.138089935299395 / 2
describe returns { n, mean, median, sd } with sd always the sample form

confidenceInterval is the normal approximation with z = 1.96 by default and NaN/NaN below two values; V8 gives 3.518379265803829 / 6.481620734196171 and [1,3] gives 0.040000000000000036 / 3.96 with no rounding
mulberry32 normalises its seed with >>> 0 and yields values in [0,1); seed 42 starts 0.6011037519201636, 0.44829055899754167, 0.8524657934904099

bootstrapCi defaults to seed 42, 1000 samples and alpha 0.05, resamples by index with the seeded generator, sorts the means and takes the floor(alpha/2 * samples) and ceil((1 - alpha/2) * samples) - 1 quantiles; V8 gives 3.625 / 6.5
bootstrapCi is deterministic: the same values, seed, sample count and alpha always return the same pair
effectSize is the pooled-sd Cohen's d with NaN below two values per group and NaN when the pooled sd is exactly 0 ([5,6,7,8] vs [1,2,3,4] gives 3.0983866769659336)
oneSampleEffectSize is (mean - baseline) / sample sd with NaN for n < 2 or sd === 0

oneSamplePermutationP defaults to seed 11 and 5000 permutations, sign-flips the baseline-centered values and returns (extreme + 1) / (permutations + 1), so the smallest attainable p-value is 1/5001 and an observed magnitude of 0 saturates at 1

permutationP defaults to 5000 permutations and seed 7 on both branches; the paired branch is NaN on unequal lengths and re-signs the within-pair differences, the unpaired branch Fisher-Yates shuffles the pooled array in place and compares the first left.length values against the rest
proportion is `of > 0 ? value / of : NaN`, so a zero or negative denominator is NaN rather than Infinity
the missing list is built in the donor's fixed order: protocol, execution-evidence, statistics, claim-graph, citation, manuscript, final-audit, then review for NOT_RUN or review-pass for VETOED

READY returns status READY and pass true only with all seven gates and a non-vetoed review, reason 'full §34 artifact chain + review approved'; otherwise pass is false, status is INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and the reason is 'fake READY caught — missing: <list>'

REJECTED passes only when the chain is complete, the review is not vetoed, replication was recorded, and either hypothesisSupported is false or the domain is negative-null-result; the donor's three reason strings are returned otherwise
REPLICATION_FAILED passes only when the chain is complete and replication is exactly 'FAILED', with reason 'replication failed and honestly recorded — PASS (no fake READY)'
INCONCLUSIVE passes when executionEvidence and statistics are both true; INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE passes when protocol and executionEvidence are both true; neither branch consults review or replication
an undeclared declaredStatus returns status INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, pass false and reason 'unknown declared status <value>', with the missing list still computed from the evidence

buildResearchBattery returns the donor's six scenarios in order (SE READY, SE fake READY, Multi-Agent null result, Reliability replication failed, Writing-evaluation inconclusive, Negative/Null insufficient evidence), covering all five domains with software-engineering twice
runResearchBattery returns the verdicts with label and expected appended, scores pass === expected, and reports passed 6 of total 6

PARITY: mean / median / standardDeviation / describe formulae, NaN guards and thresholds

the seeded mulberry32 generator and the reproducible bootstrap
the seeded one-sample sign-permutation and paired/unpaired permutation tests
Cohen's d and the one-sample effect size
the missing-item accounting and its fixed order
the READY / REJECTED / REPLICATION_FAILED / INCONCLUSIVE / INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE rules and every reason string
the six-scenario §33 battery, its labels and its self-score
